rv.q: Lovers of multi-layered scripts and dark comedy should make this a top pick for their time.
This is a roundabout way of saying the show was a lovely part of a lovely evening, and I encourage you to make this show part of an evening out on the town as well.
Newquist really digs into this role; his Michael is vile, but he somehow seems more honest after his detestable beliefs are aired than he was before.

cn.t: Critics find this dark comedy effectively exposes the thin veneer of civility separating enlightened adults from their brawling children, with strong performances driving a savage descent into primal human nature.
